sections.Astrophysical Alerts:
#### GRB 261122B: optical and radio detections establish a multiwavelength afterglow

The SVOM burst occurred on **22 November 2026 at 22:46:55 UTC**. Follow-up reported on 23–24 November adds two detections at the corrected GRB 261122B position. Kilonova-Catcher imaging began **3.5 h after the trigger**; a 12 × 300 s r-band stack, template-subtracted against Pan-STARRS, measured **r_AB = 19.83 ± 0.12** at a midpoint **4.07 h** after the trigger. This is a detection of the fading optical counterpart; the observing-program name does not classify the transient as a kilonova. [GCN 46348](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46348).

ATCA observations beginning **6.6 h after the burst** found a preliminary **≈0.2 mJy** source at **5 GHz**, positionally consistent with the optical counterpart. The report does not quote a flux uncertainty or chance-coincidence probability, and further observations were planned. [GCN 46351](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46351). Together with the earlier X-ray and optical detections, these data establish a multiwavelength afterglow. They do not by themselves determine the progenitor, redshift or energetics.

#### GRB 261119A: SVOM recovers a short burst and sharply improves its localization

Fermi/GBM first detected this event on **19 November 2026 at 19:01:35.03 UTC** and classified it as a likely short GRB with a broad **13.4° statistical localization uncertainty**. An edited SVOM report, issued 23 November and revised **24 November at 06:33:58 UTC**, describes an offline ECLAIRs detection beginning at **19:01:35.10 UTC**. The best 10–120 keV image trigger has **SNR 6.3** over **0.22 s**, too faint to trigger onboard. [GCN 46349 v2](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46349).

ECLAIRs measures **T₉₀ = 0.31 (+0.13/−0.12) s** in 4–120 keV and localizes the burst to **RA 19.059°, Dec +41.392°**, with a **12.34 arcmin 90% radius** that includes a 2 arcmin systematic contribution in quadrature. A power-law fit from T₀−0.15 to T₀+0.15 s gives photon index **−0.85 ± 0.14**, **4–120 keV fluence (9.5 ± 1.3) × 10⁻⁸ erg cm⁻²**, and photon flux **5.2 ± 0.6 photons cm⁻² s⁻¹**; the report states that these errors are 68% confidence.

This confirms that the prompt emission is short and reduces the search region dramatically relative to GBM, but short duration alone does not identify a compact-binary progenitor. No counterpart, redshift, gravitational-wave association or trials-corrected false-alarm probability is reported.

#### PKS 1958−179: renewed Fermi-LAT activity with a harder gamma-ray spectrum

Fermi-LAT reported on **23 November 2026 at 20:00 UTC** that the flat-spectrum radio quasar **PKS 1958−179** (4FGL J2000.9−1748; **z = 0.652**) entered a renewed gamma-ray high state on **22 November**. The preliminary one-day flux above 100 MeV was **(0.3 ± 0.1) × 10⁻⁶ photons cm⁻² s⁻¹**, statistical uncertainty only, about ten times the 4FGL-DR4 average. The fitted photon index was **1.7 ± 0.2**, harder than the catalogue value **2.24 ± 0.03**. [ATel 18166](https://www.astronomerstelegram.org/?read=18166).

Two photons were associated with the source at probability **>0.999** by the LAT analysis; the highest-energy event was **34 GeV** at **22 November 13:18:36 UTC**. These probabilities refer to individual photon–source associations, not the global significance of the flare. The telegram supplies no trials-corrected flare significance, contemporaneous neutrino association or causal interpretation.

#### EP261015a / SN 2026ahoa: a radio upper limit 33 days after the X-ray trigger

Einstein Probe triggered on EP261015a on **15 October 2026 at 13:15:36 UTC**; optical follow-up previously reported a broad-lined Type Ic supernova candidate, SN 2026ahoa, at tentative **z = 0.31**. ATCA observations began **17 November at 14:53 UTC**, about **33.1 days after the trigger**, with a central frequency of **8.5 GHz**. No radio source was detected at the optical position. With a local rms of **8.1 μJy beam⁻¹**, the report gives a **3σ upper limit of 24.3 μJy**. [GCN 46347](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46347).

This is a frequency- and epoch-specific upper limit. It constrains radio-emission models for the transient but does not retract the optical association, rule out radio emission at other epochs or frequencies, or establish the physical relation between the X-ray transient and the supernova.

#### EP261122a: near-infrared follow-up adds two counterpart limits

Einstein Probe/WXT triggered on EP261122a on **22 November 2026 at 06:12:37 UTC**, and FXT subsequently localized an uncatalogued X-ray source. MDM/MIRAGE observations started at **10:03:48 UTC** in J band, **3.86 h after the trigger**, and at **10:27:16 UTC** in Hs band, **4.24 h after the trigger**. No new source was found inside the FXT error circle. The reported **5σ AB limits** are **J > 19.93** for 1080 s exposure and **Hs > 19.45** for 1620 s exposure. [GCN 46350](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46350).

These measurements complement the earlier r-band limit but are shallower in AB magnitude and were obtained in different bands and at different times. They do not demonstrate that the transient lacked a counterpart, nor do they determine its source class, distance or extinction.
